items.problem: The centring remedy that closed I16's letter converted pooled dead space into left-rail drift, and on /data into a ragged left edge across four siblings on one screen. Measured by me at 1440x900 against a shell content box of 144-1296 on every route. /wiki: eyebrow, page title, lede, sort-note and the closing delisted-note all sit at x=144, and the 85-row .browse index — the page's entire purpose — is the ONLY block off the rail, at 440.1-999.9. The reader's eye jumps right for the list and back left for the note beneath it. /data: the H1 is at 144 and its four .section blocks centre independently at 617.4, 420.8, 471.2 and 580.5, each carrying its own R10-bound heading and rule with it, so four sibling section headings on one screen have four different left edges spanning 196.6px. It reads as a staircase, not as a page. /colophon: title at 144 over a body at 416, leaving a conspicuous empty 272px block directly beneath the title, which reads as a mis-indent rather than as a margin. The unoccupied width is unchanged in every case — /wiki's .browse is still 48.6% of the shell, exactly the anchor's number. Two routes prove a better remedy was available: /blog/[slug] centres its H1 and .entry-head WITH its body (all three at 416-1024), which is a conventional centred article and is not a defect; and /wiki/concept/ai-winter FILLED the freed track with FACTS (I5) rather than balancing it. /learn's untouched .rung sits left-aligned at 144-1008 at 75% occupancy and satisfies R13's occupancy clause without leaving the rail at all. Separately, /tools' two .browse surfaces are 126px and 254.3px wide inside the 1152px shell (10.9% and 22.1% occupancy, uncentred, right gaps 1026 and 897.7) — R13's occupancy clause violated on a surface neither S9 nor S13 samples, and yet those surfaces read FINE, because they keep the rail. That is the evidence that the rule is measuring the wrong property. My own iter-04 invariant is partly at fault: it offered centring as an alternative without requiring the centred block to keep the page's own rail, and the implementer satisfied it as written.

items.invariant: On every sampled route at 1440x900, the primary content block inside <main> starts within 2px of that route's own H1 and eyebrow, OR that route's H1 and eyebrow share the block's own left edge (a consistently centred article); and no two sibling section blocks within one route have left edges differing by more than 2px.
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R13 (and R13's own occupancy/centring disjunction should be amended — see prescription)
items.prescription: Return main.shell > .browse (/wiki), /data's four .section blocks and /colophon's .prose and .listing-facts to margin-inline-start: 0 so every block resumes the property's x=144 rail, and satisfy R13 the way /learn and the wiki entry already do instead: fill the freed track (S13's own 'filled' clause, which the wiki entry now passes) or accept a left-aligned narrow block as /learn's .rung does at 75% occupancy. Leave /blog/[slug] centred — its own head centres with it and that is correct. Then amend R13: replace 'occupancy >= 55% OR centred' with the property that actually matters, which is that a template's primary content block starts on the same rail as that template's own H1 and eyebrow, and that sibling blocks on one route share one left edge. Centring should be permitted only when the route's own heading matter centres with the block. Under the current disjunction /tools passes nothing and reads well while /data passes and reads badly, which is the clearest possible sign the clause is measuring the wrong thing. Extend S9/S13's route coverage to /tools, /learn, /blog and /tutorials in the same change so no template's rail is unasserted.

items.problem: S1 and S16 are ONE-SIDED in exactly JUDGE.md L4's shape, and this is the second consecutive iteration in which a check registered for R7/R13 turns out to bound only the direction the last fix moved in. Both claim to govern .browse-name's track: S1 that it 'stops before --measure-list', S16 that it 'sizes to that surface's OWN widest label, capped at --measure-list'. Run by me: `node tools/ui-invariants.mjs --only S16 --break ".browse{grid-template-columns:40px auto auto !important}"` reports ok, and the identical break against S1 reports ok. That break is not benign — I measured it live on /tools with the same injection: 42 of 47 labels wrap, the worst to 4 lines, and .browse collapses from 254.3px to 71.6px wide. A track of 40px does not size to a surface whose widest label is 131.3px, so S16's own stated property is false under a break S16 calls ok. Both checks measure only the gap between the label and the trailing track, which shrinks monotonically as the track narrows, so no track can ever be too narrow for either of them. This is L4's rule applied to a size bound rather than a collision: an invariant of the form 'this track must not be too wide' shall name the corridor the track must stay inside, not the single edge it must clear.

Re-run every S1/S16 falsifier against the post-change structure rather than transferring the old records (D8). While in there, audit S13 and S15 for the same asymmetry — S15 bounds .rail-title's track above at --measure-list and nothing bounds it below, so a 40px blog title column would also pass.

items.problem: Unchanged and re-verified by me at 1440x900: the READ column renders the identical string '2026-08-31' on 396 of 396 rows — 1 unique value, 100% share — each one an underlined link carrying the same treatment as the discriminating MODEL column, occupying 105.2px of the table's 1152px. A full column of 396 identical underlined strings is chrome by another route: it consumes a ninth of the table's width and a full column of the reader's scan while carrying zero discriminating information, and it competes for attention with IN, OUT, CONTEXT and STATUS, which are what a reader crosses the row to compare. This is the same failure R8's badge clause already forbids for status chips — drawn on every row including the unexceptional ones, so the exceptional case has nothing left to say — applied to a link treatment rather than a border. Stripe's tables state a collection-level constant once above the table and reserve per-row cells for values that discriminate; the property of Stripe's content that makes that transfer is exactly this one's, a long list of records crossed to compare a few fields.

Assert it: no column may render one value on more than 90% of rows at link weight.

items.problem: Unchanged and re-verified by me at 1440x900: every .listing child is display:block at x=144 with no grid on the listing or its container, and the four fields a reader arrives to compare — licence, pricing model, verified date and link — are still one run-on mono line separated by middots spanning the full 1152px shell.
